Local Stress: Element-Wise Constraints with Percival Solver

Description

This tutorial demonstrates local stress constraints in topology optimization. Unlike global stress aggregation (p-norm), local constraints enforce stress limits at every element individually. This provides stricter stress control but requires handling thousands of constraints efficiently.

We use Percival.jl, a specialized solver for large-scale constrained optimization, with continuation SIMP (penalty 1.0 → 3.0) to converge to stress-constrained designs.

Setup

using TopOpt, LinearAlgebra, StatsFuns
using StatsFuns: logsumexp

Define the Problem

E = 1.0 # Young's modulus
v = 0.3 # Poisson's ratio
f = 1.0 # downward force
rmin = 3.0 # filter radius

problem = PointLoadCantilever(Val{:Linear}, (160, 40), (1.0, 1.0), E, v, f)

A fine 160×40 mesh (6,400 elements) tests the solver’s ability to handle many local stress constraints.

Parameter Settings

V = 0.5        # volume fraction
xmin = 0.0001  # minimum density

x0 = fill(0.5, 160 * 40)  # initial design
N = length(x0)
penalty = TopOpt.PowerPenalty(1.0)  # start with no penalization

solver = FEASolver(DirectSolver, problem; xmin=xmin, penalty=penalty)
stress = TopOpt.von_mises_stress_function(solver)
filter = DensityFilter(solver; rmin=rmin)
volfrac = TopOpt.Volume(solver)

Local Stress Constraints

obj = x -> volfrac(filter(PseudoDensities(x))) - V  # volume constraint as objective
thr = 150  # stress threshold

# Local constraints: (σᵢ - thr)/N ≤ 0 for each element
constr = x -> begin
    s = stress(filter(PseudoDensities(x)))
    return (s .- thr) / length(s)
end

Each element’s von Mises stress must satisfy the threshold. The constraint function returns a vector (one constraint per element), which Percival handles efficiently using interior-point methods.

Optimization with Continuation

alg = PercivalAlg()
options = PercivalOptions(; max_iter=10, subsolver_max_eval=50)
model = Model(obj)
addvar!(model, zeros(N), ones(N))
add_ineq_constraint!(model, constr)

x = copy(x0)
for p in [1.0, 3.0]
    TopOpt.setpenalty!(solver, p)
    global r = optimize(model, alg, x; options=options)
    global x = r.minimizer
    println("Penalty $p: obj=$(obj(x)), max_stress=$(maximum(stress(filter(PseudoDensities(x)))))")
end

The continuation strategy (penalty 1.0 → 3.0) helps converge to feasible designs by first solving a relaxed problem.

Verify Results

@show maximum(stress(filter(PseudoDensities(x0))))  # initial max stress
@show maximum(stress(filter(PseudoDensities(x))))   # final max stress

# Verify peak stress doesn't exceed threshold by more than 5%
s = stress(filter(PseudoDensities(x)))
println("Stress constraint satisfied: $((maximum(s) - thr) / thr < 0.05)")
maximum(stress(filter(PseudoDensities(x0)))) = 4.873821547967778
maximum(stress(filter(PseudoDensities(x)))) = 151.33656937112656
Stress constraint satisfied: true

Visualization

using CairoMakie
fig = visualize(
    problem;
    topology=r.minimizer,
    default_exagg_scale=0.07,
    scale_range=10.0,
    vector_arrowsize=0.5,
)

The optimized design shows smooth stress distributions without concentration points, demonstrating effective local stress control.
